state: prospectively fixed before this group's Q6 flux was inspected; exploratory independent source cohort; parameters held fixed throughout
science_question: Does a local photometric recurrence safeguard distinguish repeat stellar eclipse-like dips from nonperiodic instrumental changes when applied to the existing November 7 sudden-step heuristic, without inappropriately protecting verified instrument events?
selection_rule: Eight published Kepler eclipsing binaries/circumbinary-planet hosts and five separately confirmed single-host transiting-planet examples, named by literature before running this cohort. Disjoint from Kepler-47, documented KIC7461601 SPSD and the earlier Q6 preselected cohort and Q8 six-star step study. ALL unavailable files remain in denominator; no replacements.
data: MAST original Kepler Quarter 6 long-cadence FITS. Read original TIME, SAP_FLUX, PDCSAP_FLUX, SAP_QUALITY with joint-valid positive finite pairing; retain original quality-flagged points for instrument diagnostic; no planet discovery claims.
original_step_rule: Identical unchanged localized_downward_step_mask() and preprocessing block from LOCALIZED_STEP_STUDY_FROZEN_2026_11_07.json, with no epoch supplied. Never call archival label until after warnings are calculated.

recurrence_guard.definition: At each original detected step onset, scan fixed periods and compare short-dip evidence in independent repeated cycle windows using only normalized flux/time, with no published ephemerides or source roles. A protected warning is retained as evidence but the local destructive mask is suppressed.
recurrence_guard.freeze_against_reuse: No tuning on Kepler-47 or the old 12-star cohort after new observational outcomes; 2026-11-08 code and parameters fixed before first new flux experiment.

metrics: all planned source counts and file failures
archival bit1024 event counts and matched warnings, if present
raw warnings count and guarded count on both SAP and PDCSAP
warning-level periodic evidence and scan period
binary versus planet-host counts only descriptively; not a valid instrument FAP estimate
cadences spared by guard (not equivalent to confirmed real signals)
number of archival positive instrument events incorrectly protected, if any
limitations: Repetition guard will fail on long periods with fewer than 4 observed eclipse cycles in Q6; several of the named stars have published periods above 22 days and are deliberately retained as difficult cases.
Published binary orbital periods/roles are reserved for post-hoc description and not given to recurrence search.
Confirmed planet host label does not imply absence of binary or instrumental contaminants.
Confirmed binaries are purposely selected and not a random sample of Kepler data.
Quality bit1024 labels are incomplete and may be absent; do not claim precision/FAP from unmatched warnings.
Period-grid multiple testing creates risk of spurious recurrence; offline controls and independent sources must be evaluated.
This method protects data rather than identifying planets; improved cadences retained do not establish higher planet recall.
